Messages.Author: shawn stanley
Messages.Body:
Card text first and then the question, which might be out of the realm
of the bleeding obvious, but it would be nice o hve it clarified.

Extremis Boon
Master: out-of-turn.
Only usable when you are being ousted. Other Methuselahs may bid pool
to keep you in the game. If one does, put this card in play. as a
master phase action, the high bidder may steal up to 2 pool from you.
You may burn this card by giving that Methuselah 6 pool during your
master phase.

So, the question ... or statements really. Presumably you get the
amount of pool bid from the highest bidder rather than just being left
in the game without any pool. Or do you get the pool from everyone's
bid but only the highest bidding Methuselah get's the benefit?

Extremis Boon

Master: out-of-turn.
Only usable when you are being ousted. Other Methuselahs may bid pool

to keep you in the game. Move the winning bid (if any) to your pool, and put
this card in play. (While this card is in play) the high bidder may steal up
to 2 pool from you as a master phase action.

You may burn this card by giving that Methuselah 6 pool during your
master phase.

I think it's unnecessary to try to prevent the card from being put in play
if there are no bids (like the current text does), because the player is
ousted by then and so the card is burned with no effect anyway.

While we're at it: is the '...to keep you in the game' text binding, ie,
must any bid be at least enough to keep you in the game? Or is it possible
(for example) to bid 1 when at least 3 pool is necessary to keep the player
in the game? (Obviously the player would be ousted anyway and the pool is
lost, but I'm sure someone will come up with a situation where it's
advantageous.)

Flux

> "where does the pool come from?" question.

Since it's the other methuselahs that bid from their pool, and that bid is
explicitly moved to you pool, it seems clear enough for me. But you can
improve that with another small change:

'... Move the winning bid (if any) from the winner's pool to your pool, ...'

It does become somewhat stilted though.

Another option:

'...Other Methuselahs may bid from their pool to keep you in the game. ...'

> There's always someone who will contest the clarity or unambiguity of
> a given card text.

Agreed. :)

>> While we're at it: is the '...to keep you in the game' text binding,
>> ie, must any bid be at least enough to keep you in the game? Or is it
>
>
> Yes. Card text.

Ok.
That means this text serves two functions: it identifies where the bidding
pool goes to and it places a minimum on the bids.

IMO it's best to avoid such text, because many people will only look for one
meaning to the text and stop at that. If/when they identify the secondary
meaning, they'll then be left wondering if this secondary meaning is
intended or accidental. At least I did. :)

Flux

Actually I already had a discussion about this.

One take is that other meth's bid pool and the pool bid goes to the
blood bank, while the person being ousted simply treats the ousting
effect as having been canceled.

So a 6 bleed against a player with 6 or less pool remains at the pool
they started that action with. Its kind of link playing a DI after the
fact and the other meths get to pay the cost.

So yea. The card text could use a refinement.
